minutes.headline: Planning Board waived site plan review for a Gatsby Grounds sign and put master plan ranking off to July 22.
minutes.summary: The board granted a sign waiver at 493 Mass Ave, approved ten sets of minutes, and heard committee reports. Most of the meeting was a long debate over how to use master plan money, with some members wanting visioning sessions and a review of past plans before an RFP. The board also discussed a possible Economic Development Committee, Open Space vacancies, a Stone Farm bond, and Unitil tree clearing, and nominated a member as MRPC representative.

votes.motion: Grant the waiver request for 493 Massachusetts Ave sign; a member recused.
Approve all minutes from April 22 to June 10, 2019 with the scrivener's edit to 4/22.
Nominate Mrs. Bertram as the board's MRPC representative.

budget_items.what_was_said: The capital plan holds master plan money that will not cover a complete plan; a matching grant was applied for with no word yet.
Staff gave a rough per-chapter cost, with open space cheaper because the work is done.
Remaining punch list work may be paid by claiming the developer's bond; staff noted a local contractor might do it for less than the prevailing-wage estimate.

decisions.decision: Economic development committee discussion set for the first meeting in August (August 12); master plan discussion first on July 22.
Staff to seek sample master plan RFPs and resend the open space plan; board to meet July 22 rather than earlier.
Staff will advertise the two Open Space ad hoc vacancies and close applications the week before July 22.
July 8 agenda to start off-street parking and solar bylaw discussion; earth removal also on it.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board put off ranking master plan chapters and the RFP to its July 22 meeting after a long debate over how to use the money.
The board took up a sign waiver for 493 Mass Ave (Gatsby Grounds) with one member recused; the minutes record the vote outcome as not audible.
The board voted unanimously to nominate Mrs. Bertram as its representative to the MRPC.
An Economic Development Committee discussion was set for August 12, after master plan discussion on July 22.
Staff will advertise two Open Space ad hoc vacancies, and the Stone Farm punch list may be paid by claiming the developer's bond.

why_it_matters: Master plan money in the capital plan will not cover a complete plan, so the choices on chapters and visioning decide how much planning the town gets and whether it needs more funding, possibly at Town Meeting.
Claiming the Stone Farm bond could finish unfinished road work without the town budget, mostly taxes, covering the cost.
watch_next: July 22: master plan discussion and chapter ranking resume, with sample RFPs and the open space plan from staff.
August 12: first discussion of an Economic Development Committee.
